headlines.text: Firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says. Pete Hegseth says the execution will be public, but a legal expert says the "unprecedented" decision is on "uncertain legal terrain".
Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC. Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.
ICE agent shoots man in New York City. The mayor of New York expressed outrage at the shooting which the Department of Homeland Security said happened during the arrest of a "criminal illegal alien".

Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge. Ukraine accused Russia of targeting two crowded vehicles in the front line city of Kramatorsk to kill as many civilians as possible.
Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis. Hundreds have pitched their tents in central Madrid, while the Spanish prime minister has called a snap election.
Cars torched and shops looted as anti-migrant violence erupts in South Africa. South Africa has experienced recurrent outbreaks of violence, often targeting migrants from neighbouring countries.

Russian strikes and approaching winter force many in Kyiv to pack bags and flee. A renewed Russian campaign of strikes on power and energy infrastructure has made some contemplate leaving Ukraine's capital.
Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design. The German sportswear brand wants the Sydney-based label to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.
'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize. Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.
Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture. The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.
Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation. Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani had been secretly released on parole in 2025, after serving less than half his sentence.

Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.
US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says. More than 500 migrants have been expelled from the US to African countries, HRW says, citing US data.
Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar dies suddenly at 75. Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.
Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile. The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.
Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize. International Court of Justice judge Navi Pillay has been awarded this year’s Nobel Peace Prize.
Everton’s US owners seek sale of controlling stake in Premier League club. Premier League club Everton open to selling controlling stake after 'safely' balancing historical financial troubles.

Japan’s Okinawa calls for review of US forces pact after killing. Assembly on the island, where tens of thousands of US soldiers are stationed, seeks change after Marine arrested.
LeBron James stars in NBA preseason debut but Nets defeat 76ers. All-time leading scorer LeBron James makes 76ers debut following LA Lakers switch in NBA preseason, but Nets claim win.
US ICE releases Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh from custody. Award-winning filmmaker, detained last month, is released on bond with next hearing set for October 27, campaign says.
Three years after October 7, prolonged war takes its toll on Israelis. Children’s psychiatric emergency visits have more than doubled in Israel, study shows.
Why has Iraq decided to ban online map service Waze?. Iraq plans to ban Waze, citing Israeli origins, and suggests alternatives like Google Maps or local app in development.
Who is Dov Lando, the Israeli rabbi criticising Zionism?. The senior rabbi, whose party is in Netanyahu's coalition, has caused uproar in Israel by calling Zionism disastrous.
Afghanistan’s emerald miners struggle with tools but attract global buyers. Afghan miners endure harsh conditions, relying on basic tools to extract precious emeralds in Panjshir's steep valleys.
Trump says US will not strike Iran before midterm elections. Oil prices drop as Trump dismisses speculation of pre-midterm military action against Iran.
Brazilian Supreme Court judge issues arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro. Arrest warrant for presidential candidate's brother is issued weeks before Brazil's runoff election.
From Aden to Sanaa, Yemenis struggle to deal with soaring living costs. As fighting intensifies, Yemenis face a deepening economic crisis, with unpaid salaries and rising prices.

Schumer says he's not going anywhere, but his own candidates aren't ready to back him. Chuck Schumer told Politico he is running for re-election as leader, but candidates like Adam Hamilton and Sen. Elissa Slotkin want fresh leadership.

Democrats say they'll make life affordable. Your wallet may disagree. Democrats are pushing affordability as their 2026 message, but a financial advisor asks whether subsidies actually lower costs or just shift the bill.

Creators of October 7 play call fire alarm disruption at Northwestern a 'cowardly' attempt at intimidation. A fire alarm disrupted the play "OCTOBER 7" at Northwestern University's Cahn Auditorium, but defiant audience members returned to give a standing ovation.

Mamdani demands Trump release illegal immigrant shot by ICE agent as protests erupt in the Bronx. Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded President Donald Trump release the man shot and injured by an ICE agent on Thursday in an incident that set off protests across New York City.

Guardians force decisive ALDS Game 5 as White Sox miss chance to reach first ALCS since 2005. White Sox-Guardians ALDS Game 4 saw Cleveland erupt for two fifth-inning home runs to erase Chicago's lead and force a decisive Game 5 Saturday.

Brian Schottenheimer now sits on hottest seat in NFL after Cowboys collapse against Buccaneers. Bucky Irving's 72-yard run sparked a Tampa Bay Buccaneers comeback as rookie Jalon Daniels led the charge to upset the Dallas Cowboys at home.

A'ja Wilson wins record fifth MVP as first three-peat in WNBA history strengthens all-time greatness case. The Las Vegas Aces star's fifth WNBA MVP puts her alongside Bill Russell, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Michael Jordan in rarefied historic air.

Tony Romo got disqualified from his Korn Ferry qualifier the same day he 'parted ways' with CBS Sports. Tony Romo was disqualified from a Korn Ferry Tour pre-qualifier for signing an incorrect scorecard on the same day he parted ways with CBS Sports.

Rumbling volcano forces immediate trail closures at popular vacation hot spot. The Kīlauea volcano shows renewed spattering at two vents as USGS scientists monitor for a possible 55th episode of lava fountains at the summit.

2 foreign nationals breach UK base housing key US, NATO intel hub amid $556M expansion. The Latvian men were arrested under the National Security Act 2023 after breaching a fence at RAF Molesworth, prompting a major counterterrorism investigation.

Federal grand jury hears evidence in probe of former Trump aide Cassidy Hutchinson's Jan 6 testimony: source. A federal grand jury heard evidence about possible false statements Cassidy Hutchinson made to the Jan. 6 House select committee on the Capitol riot.

Luka Dončić says he 'definitely' regrets playing through hamstring injury that ended his season. Luka Dončić revealed he felt a hamstring tweak against the Oklahoma City Thunder but pushed through, a decision he says cost the Lakers a title.

Michigan Senate debate erupts into personal attacks as Rogers, El-Sayed clash over Israel, Iran and more. Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed clashed in their first head-to-head public debate during a fiery showdown Thursday night filled with personal attacks and accusations.

Missouri football's Johnnie 'DJ' Jones recovering after successful heart transplant, coach says. Johnnie "DJ" Jones underwent heart transplant surgery Wednesday after Mayo Clinic doctors in Jacksonville detected a serious cardiac condition.

Arizona man arrested after allegedly emailing White House bomb threat to Tucson news station. Jacob Aaron Hicks allegedly emailed a Tucson news station claiming an imminent bomb strike against the White House, prompting an FBI investigation.

ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work. A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.
